source: TSTD / ADB TA 7305-CAM technical manual, "សណ្តែកត្រើង (សណ្តែកកួរ)" [Yard-long bean cultivation manual]
text: A major focus of this manual is trellising/staking, since yard-long bean is a climbing vine that produces much better yield and pod quality when grown vertically on a support structure rather than left to sprawl on the ground. The manual describes building a trellis or stake system before or shortly after planting so vines have support to climb as soon as they start reaching, and explains that trellised plants get better light exposure, air circulation (reducing fungal disease pressure), and cleaner pods (less soil contact and rot) than ground-grown plants, translating directly into higher marketable yield.
